tokens.name: surface
tokens.usage: Page background. The instrument's bench: quiet so pictures and numbers carry the screen.

tokens.name: surface-raised
tokens.usage: Panels, cards, lineage nodes, diff cards.

tokens.name: surface-sunken
tokens.usage: Wells behind puzzle grids and charts, and neutral badges.

tokens.name: line
tokens.usage: Hairlines, panel borders, chart grid lines.

tokens.name: line-strong
tokens.usage: Control borders and dashed rejected-node borders; 3:1 against surface-raised in both themes.

tokens.name: ink
tokens.usage: Primary text and numbers on surface, surface-raised and surface-sunken.

tokens.name: ink-muted
tokens.usage: Labels, axis text, metadata. 4.5:1 or better on every surface in both themes.

tokens.name: accent
tokens.usage: Signal teal. Selection, the active generation, focus rings, links. As text on surface, surface-raised or accent-soft.

tokens.name: accent-soft
tokens.usage: Tinted ground behind accent text (running badge, selected row).

tokens.name: on-accent
tokens.usage: Text on an accent fill (primary button label).

tokens.name: good
tokens.usage: Gate passed, positive deltas. As text on the surfaces or good-soft.

tokens.name: good-soft
tokens.usage: Ground behind good text.

tokens.name: warn
tokens.usage: Budget or deadline warnings. As text on the surfaces or warn-soft.

tokens.name: warn-soft
tokens.usage: Ground behind warn text.

tokens.name: critical
tokens.usage: Rejected mutations, negative deltas, database read denied. As text on the surfaces or critical-soft.

tokens.name: critical-soft
tokens.usage: Ground behind critical text.

tokens.name: series-train
tokens.usage: Training-set score line. Alias of accent so the active thing and the optimized thing share a color.

tokens.name: series-heldout
tokens.usage: Held-out score line. Burnt orange against teal: separable in lightness and for red-green color blindness.

tokens.name: series-baseline
tokens.usage: Baseline reference, always drawn dashed.

tokens.name: px-void
tokens.usage: Puzzle palette 0. Image content only; never UI state. Same in both themes.

tokens.name: px-paper
tokens.usage: Puzzle palette 1. Image content only.

tokens.name: px-red
tokens.usage: Puzzle palette 2. Image content only.

tokens.name: px-orange
tokens.usage: Puzzle palette 3. Image content only.

tokens.name: px-yellow
tokens.usage: Puzzle palette 4. Image content only.

tokens.name: px-green
tokens.usage: Puzzle palette 5. Image content only. Lighter than px-red and darker than px-orange, so neighbors on the red-green axis separate in lightness.

tokens.name: px-blue
tokens.usage: Puzzle palette 6. Image content only.

tokens.name: px-brown
tokens.usage: Puzzle palette 7. Image content only.

styles.name: display
styles.usage: One per screen at most: the product name or the headline number on a slide.

styles.name: body
styles.sample: The harness suppressed two sensors that overstate their reliability.

styles.name: small
styles.sample: Scored for display only, never used for selection.

styles.name: label
styles.usage: Uppercase labels: genome knobs, axis titles, node headers. Set text-transform: uppercase.

styles.name: num
styles.usage: Scores, deltas, latencies, counts, genome values. Always tabular-nums.

tokens.name: space-1
tokens.usage: Gaps inside a chip or between a number and its unit.

tokens.name: space-2
tokens.usage: Gaps between related items; badge padding.

tokens.name: space-4
tokens.usage: Panel padding; gaps between cards.

tokens.name: space-6
tokens.usage: Gaps between panels and sections.

tokens.name: cell
tokens.usage: Default pixel-cell size: a 16x16 puzzle is 192px square. Showcase grids use 2x (24px).

tokens.name: radius-cell
tokens.usage: Pixel cells. Always square; a rounded pixel is a different picture.

tokens.name: radius-sm
tokens.usage: Badges, small markers.

tokens.name: radius-md
tokens.usage: Lineage nodes, buttons, inputs.

tokens.name: radius-lg
tokens.usage: Panels and diff cards.

tokens.name: conf-floor
tokens.usage: Cell opacity at confidence 0. Opacity = conf-floor + (1 - conf-floor) x confidence, so an unsure pixel is faint but never gone.
